description: Rank member/position groups by their share of all attendance and return exactly 10 rows, cutting arbitrarily through any tie at 10th place.

b.request: Group attendance records by member ID and position, count records in each group, divide each count by the total number of attendance records, and return exactly 10 groups with member ID, position, count, and share, ordered by share descending and breaking ties arbitrarily
b.sql: SELECT a.link_to_member AS member_id, m.position, COUNT(*) AS count, COUNT(*) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM attendance) AS share FROM attendance AS a JOIN member AS m ON m.member_id = a.link_to_member GROUP BY a.link_to_member, m.position ORDER BY share DESC LIMIT 10;

c.request: Which are the top 10 members by share of total event attendance? Match attendance to members by member id, count attendance per member id and position, and show the member id, position, attendance count and share of all attendance, from highest share to lowest. Rank member/position groups by their share of all attendance and return exactly 10 rows, cutting arbitrarily through any tie at 10th place.
c.sql: SELECT m.member_id, m.position, COUNT(*) AS attendance_count, COUNT(*) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM attendance) AS attendance_share FROM attendance AS a JOIN member AS m ON a.link_to_member = m.member_id GROUP BY m.member_id, m.position ORDER BY attendance_share DESC, m.member_id LIMIT 10;

a.request: Matching each attendance record to its member by member id (dropping attendance with no matching member), count the attendance records for each member id and `position` combination, and work out each count as a share of the total of all these counts. List the member id, position, attendance count and share, sorted by share from highest to lowest, and return exactly 10 rows. If there is a tie at 10th place, keep only as many of the tied rows as fit, chosen arbitrarily.
a.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT m.member_id, m.position, COUNT(*) AS attendance_count FROM attendance AS a JOIN member AS m ON a.link_to_member = m.member_id GROUP BY m.member_id, m.position) SELECT member_id, position, attendance_count, 1.0 * attendance_count / SUM(attendance_count) OVER () AS share FROM counts ORDER BY share DESC LIMIT 10;

d.request: Which 10 member ID and position groups have the highest share of total event attendance? Match attendance to members by member ID, count attendance for each member ID and position, and return the member ID, position, attendance count, and share of all attendance in descending share order. Return exactly 10 rows, breaking any tie at 10th place arbitrarily.
d.sql: SELECT m.member_id, m.position, COUNT(*) AS attendance_count, COUNT(*) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM attendance) AS attendance_share FROM attendance AS a JOIN member AS m ON a.link_to_member = m.member_id GROUP BY m.member_id, m.position ORDER BY attendance_share DESC LIMIT 10;
